sections.title: Description
sections.html:
This 3.3° by 2.2° field shows M33, the Triangulum Galaxy, the third large galaxy of the Local Group after Andromeda and the Milky Way. It lies about 2.7 million light-years away and spans more than a degree, twice the apparent diameter of the Moon.

M33 is a spiral seen almost face-on, with loose, flocculent arms. Their blue tint comes from countless young, hot stars; the yellower centre is populated by older stars. The arms are dotted with pink spots: regions of ionized hydrogen where stars are born, brought out by the Ha filter. The largest, NGC 604, is one of the biggest stellar nurseries known in nearby galaxies.

The rest of the field shows the stars of our own Galaxy, in the foreground, and a few very faint veils of galactic dust.

The colours are close to the real ones: they were calibrated on the stars in the field, and the hydrogen only reinforces the red.

This image was acquired in collaboration with Renaud Venne-Landry.

sections.title: Processing
sections.html:
Done entirely in PixInsight 1.9.6, starting from the raw frames.

Preprocessing (per filter)

  • Calibration: 180 s and 600 s master darks at 0 °C; L, R, G, B and Ha master flats at 0 °C.
  • Frame alignment, local normalization, stacking.
  • Astrometric solution of each stack.

Preparation

  • RGB combination and colour calibration on the stars in the field (SpectrophotometricColorCalibration, Gaia catalogue).
  • Common cropping of the edges.

Linear processing

  • Light gradient correction (AutomaticBackgroundExtractor, degree-1 polynomial).
  • BlurXTerminator (deconvolution), NoiseXTerminator (noise reduction), StarXTerminator (separation of the stars from the nebulae).

Non-linear processing

  • Background neutralization, then linked stretch of the three colours, target background level 0.20.
  • Colour saturation boosted in the galaxy only (luminosity mask), before combining with the luminance, which otherwise washes it out.
  • Ha injected into the red and into the luminance.
  • Combination of the luminance with the colour (LRGB).
  • Centre compression: HDRMultiscaleTransform (8 layers, applied at 80%), with a luminosity mask.
  • Green toned down (SCNR 0.7), contrast and saturation curves.
  • Reintegration of the stars, stretched less than the nebulae.

Notes

  • Fourth version of the rendering. The first two showed a grey, flat galaxy: compression with 6 layers erased its relief.
  • DarkStructureEnhance was not applied (it digs a dark halo around galaxies).
  • The edge of the galaxy remains a little sharp against the background, and the lower corners keep a slight magenta tint (leftover gradient).
  • Final adjustments made by hand in PixInsight.
